Sandbox_OE_QuietHornEnable_tooltip: Stops the vehicle horn attracting zombies. The horn still sounds normally for everyone nearby, and each vehicle keeps its own horn; it simply no longer makes a noise the dead can walk toward, so it cannot be used to herd a crowd off a street. Affects the horn only - the engine, the alarm and the reversing beeper are untouched. Turn off to restore vanilla, immediately and without a restart.
Sandbox_OE_RipItEnable_tooltip: Adds Rip All to the right-click menu, in both your inventory and the world. It works on the containers you currently have open - your own bags plus whatever is in the loot window - and never reaches further than that. Covers cloth, denim and leather clothing plus sheets; leather garments yield strips. Speed is set on the Action Speed page.
Sandbox_OE_LumberjackEnable_tooltip: Master toggle for wooden-item weight scaling. Turning it off restores the vanilla weights exactly - the original values are kept, so nothing drifts however many times the dials are changed. Takes effect at the next world load.
Sandbox_OE_LumberjackBulkWeight_tooltip: Multiplier against the VANILLA weight of the material you haul: logs, log stacks, planks, firewood, firewood bundles and twigs. 1.0 is vanilla, 0.5 is half. Vanilla for reference: a log is 9.0 and a plank 3.0, which is most of an inventory before you carry anything useful.
Sandbox_OE_LumberjackWoodWeight_tooltip: Multiplier against the VANILLA weight of everything else the game itself treats as burnable wood - the items that can be turned into charcoal. Defaults to 1.0 (vanilla) on purpose: the usual complaint is hauling building material, not carrying a baseball bat. Modded items that use the same tags are covered automatically.
Sandbox_OE_LumberjackSweepEnable_tooltip: Adds "Chop nearby trees" to the world right-click menu, which fells them one after another instead of asking you to click each one. Vanilla already swings until a single tree falls; this is only about moving on to the next, and about stopping sensibly.
Sandbox_OE_LumberjackSweepRadius_tooltip: How far out the sweep looks for trees. Nearest are felled first, so a sweep cut short leaves clear ground around you rather than a scatter of stumps at the edges.
Sandbox_OE_LumberjackSweepAxeFloor_toolt: Stop the sweep when the axe drops to this fraction of its condition. 0.05 is five percent. Checked between trees, never mid-swing, so a sweep never abandons a half-felled trunk.
Sandbox_OE_LumberjackSweepEnduranceFloor: Stop the sweep when endurance drops this low, so you can still walk home. Without a floor the sweep does not pause politely: every remaining swing fails the game's own endurance check instantly and the whole sweep evaporates with trees still standing.
Sandbox_OE_ContainerOrderEnable_tooltip: Lets players drag the container buttons down the left of their own inventory into whatever order they like, and keeps that order as they change bags. It is stored per character and nothing moves until a player drags something themselves. Turn this off if the collection includes a container mod that arranges those same buttons - Better Containers and Clean UI both do - so the two are not deciding the order at once.
Sandbox_OE_InventoryCollapseEnable_toolt: Adds Equipped and Hotbar buttons to the control row under a player's own inventory, each folding that block of items out of the list so only loose gear is shown. The two fold independently and the choice is remembered per character; nothing is hidden until a player presses one. Turn this off if the collection includes a UI mod that rearranges that control row - Clean UI does - so the buttons are not competing for space in it.
Sandbox_OE_StickyHeadwearEnable_tooltip: Stops your worn headwear being knocked off when you take a hit. Applies to the items you are wearing, not to the item definitions, so zombies still spawn with the usual share of missing hats and the loot table is unchanged. Switching this off restores the original values without a restart.
Sandbox_OE_ActionSpeedEnable_tooltip: Master switch for timed-action speed scaling (default ON). Each family below picks a speed from Vanilla up to Instant. Inventory transfers are never scaled - in multiplayer the server completes them on vanilla timing, so speeding the client only makes the progress bar lie. Sandbox changes require a server restart.
Sandbox_OE_ASCleaning_tooltip: Cleaning blood, burns and graffiti; washing yourself and clothing.
Sandbox_OE_ASRepair_tooltip: Repairing clothing, vehicle engines and light bars.
Sandbox_OE_ASHood_tooltip: The wait between popping the hood and the mechanics screen appearing (vanilla: about 200 ticks at Mechanics 0, shrinking to nothing at level 15). This dial ONLY covers that wait - the work you do once the screen is open has its own separate setting below, so a fast hood does not make part swapping instant. The hood door swing itself is animation-driven and stays vanilla length.
Sandbox_OE_ASMechanics_tooltip: Bench work on the mechanics screen: installing and uninstalling parts, fixing parts, and taking engine parts. Opening the hood has its own separate setting above. Fuel and tire filling are never scaled: their duration IS the fluid transfer, so speeding them only makes the bar lie.
Sandbox_OE_ASRipIt_tooltip: Ripping clothing and sheets into rags and strips, cutting up belts, and cutting tanned hides into leather strips. Applies to those recipes wherever they are run, so the vanilla craft panel is scaled by this dial too - not just RIPIT's Rip All and Cut All.
Sandbox_OE_ASThread_tooltip: Picking thread out of ripped sheets or denim strips at a needle, awl or tweezers - the PickThread and PickAramidThread recipes. Vanilla takes about 1000 ticks at Tailoring 1, easing to 800 by Tailoring 5. This dial covers those two recipes only: no other crafting is touched, because everything hand-crafted in Build 42 shares one action and speeding that would speed forging and cooking too.
